title: Choose the visual world for Ality Intelligence
question: The roll assigned Safe Water (offshore buoyage marks). Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. All three keep your contour-and-nodes background and the turbine-graph logo.

options.label: Safe Water
options.lineage: IALA buoyage: cardinal, lateral and safe-water marks every offshore crew reads
options.thesis: Ality marks where a supplier and a project can meet safely, in the colour system offshore people already trust.
options.viewport: Pale chart-sea ground with your animated contours and linking nodes; wide grotesk headline; the main action sits on a yellow-and-black cardinal band.
options.risk: Buoy yellow shouts; scattered around it reads as a site-safety sign rather than a brand.

raised.raise: Every section is named and numbered like a chart's list of marks.
States commit totally: a chosen item floods with its mark colour, nothing half-tinted.
One unbroken contour line runs the full page as its reading spine.
The three-step explanation draws itself on as the visitor reaches it.
One label grid (name, code, value) rules every card on the site.

options.label: Admiralty Chart
options.thesis: The site is a working sea chart: depth tints, soundings and a graticule border frame every page.
options.viewport: The hero is the chart itself: contours over depth tints, lat/long ticks round the edge, magenta notice for the main action.
options.risk: The most expected reading of your contour idea; can look like a GIS app if the type is timid.

options.label: Night Wake
options.lineage: bioluminescent plankton lighting a ship's wake at night
options.thesis: Links light up like plankton wherever two contour nodes meet, then fade back to dark sea.
options.viewport: Black sea field; contours glow faintly and flare blue where the pointer passes; white headline over it.
options.case: Holds on audience (offshore at night is real to them); loses on clarity, the mood outweighs the offer.
options.risk: Dark-with-glow is a common AI look; procurement readers may find it moody rather than trustworthy.

options.label: Lotería Night
options.thesis: Each capability a numbered picture card.
options.case: Fuses poorly: energy engineers do not see themselves in a party game.
options.kept: Every item named and numbered in the same breath.

options.label: Racing League
options.viewport: Liveried hero racing left to right.
options.case: Fuses poorly: speed is the wrong promise for careful qualification.
options.kept: Total state commitment: selection floods with colour.

options.label: Step Row
options.thesis: The assessment as a programmed sequence.
options.viewport: Sixteen-step row as the page spine.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no link to energy or supply chains.
options.kept: One unbroken line as the page's spine.

options.label: Napkin Zine
options.thesis: Explain fit assessment like a friend's sketch.
options.case: Fuses poorly: too casual for confidential commercial work.
options.kept: Explanation drawn on step by step.

options.label: Box Stacks
options.thesis: Suppliers as labelled boxes on a wall.
options.case: Fuses poorly: retail collecting is far from offshore procurement.
options.kept: One label grid ruling every card.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What supply-chain intelligence companies ship, executed well.
canonCard.viewport: Navy hero with a network visual, headline left, demo button, logo row below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Altana, Everstream and the old site by design.
